author: Dr. Sarah Miller, MD
content: SOAP NOTE - Encounter Date: 2025-08-10. Subjective: 47-year-old male presents for 6-month hypertension follow-up. Reports mild occasional headaches and mild exertion dyspnea. Adherence to Lisinopril is consistent. Objective: BP 138/88 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, SpO2 98% on room air. BMI 28.4. Lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally. Heart: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs. Assessment: Essential hypertension, suboptimally controlled; Stage 1. Plan: Increase Lisinopril from 10mg daily to 20mg daily orally. Order basic metabolic panel (BMP) to check electrolytes and creatinine in 4 weeks. Return for BP check in 6 weeks.

author: Dr. Kevin Vance, MD
content: SOAP NOTE - Encounter Date: 2025-07-15. Subjective: 39-year-old female presents with seasonal allergic rhinitis, sneezing, nasal congestion, and itchy watery eyes for 3 weeks. No fever or purulent drainage. Known severe allergy to Penicillin (causes hives/anaphylaxis). Objective: Vital signs stable, afebrile. HEENT: Pale, boggy nasal turbinates with clear rhinorrhea. Conjunctival injection bilaterally. Assessment: Moderate allergic rhinitis. Plan: Start Fluticasone propionate nasal spray 50mcg, 2 sprays per nostril once daily. Cetirizine 10mg daily as needed. Strict avoidance of Penicillin and beta-lactam class antibiotics noted in chart.
